meet.helpBcBody:
This is a broadcast: one host (and anyone they call up) on the Stage, and everyone else watching. Two people or a full room, it runs the same — every phone talks only to a handful of neighbors, and the broadcast reaches everyone.

Watching

  • The link is all you need. Your camera and microphone are not used — watching asks no permissions at all.
  • The video stays blurred until the host sets a room password. If you’re asked for one, the host shares it separately — it’s the ticket, and it does not ride the link.
  • Chat is live to everyone here, is not stored on any server, and is gone when the broadcast ends.
  • Sound on on the room bar mutes the stage on this device. Everyone else still hears it.

Speaking up

  • Tap Raise hand to ask for the Stage. The host can call you up — your own phone then asks for your camera and mic (your choice to grant), and you join the host on Stage for the whole room.
  • Step off is yours to do at any time; the host can also take the Stage back.

For the host

  • Your host password is yours alone — it IS your control of this broadcast. Do not send it to viewers.
  • The Password button sets or changes the room password: without one the broadcast stays blurred; with one, whoever you give it to sees you clear.
  • The hand queue floats to the top — tap a name to call them up on Stage. Revoking their grant pulls them back down.
  • Chat has a Turn chat off switch (your messages still land) and per-message delete. Ban lives on each tile’s controls.
  • A broadcast lives while its host is present. End it, and everyone watching sees a five-minute countdown, then the room closes.

Underneath it is the same thing as a GifOS Meeting: everything goes straight between the people here, no accounts, no company keeping your video.
meet.helpAppBody:
This room exists around a shared app: everyone here sees and uses the same live app together — moves, edits and state flow between every phone directly.

The app is the show

  • The app fills the screen. One person hosts it (their device runs its engine); everyone else interacts live.
  • If the host drops off, what happens is the room’s choice at creation: an owned app pauses until its owner returns; a resilient one lets a friend still here take over hosting.

No camera

  • This room has no camera and no video. Nothing here is blurred, because there is no picture to blur.
  • Talk, when the host turns it on, is voice only. You can use the app and chat without joining it.

Chat, files, invites

  • Chat stays between the people here — no server ever sees it; it’s gone when the room empties.
  • Files can be pinned once the room has a password.
  • Invite copies the one link that brings a friend straight in. The link is the whole key — share it deliberately.

Underneath it is the same thing as a GifOS Meeting: everything goes straight between the people here, no accounts, no limit on how many.
meet.helpMeetBody:
This meeting has no size limit. The dream: the whole Earth in one meeting at once — everyone able to speak. Your phone talks only to a handful of neighbors.

The room

  • Stage — step up to be seen and heard first by the whole room. Tap again to step down.
  • Row — the people next to you.
  • The stadium — everyone else, one mosaic and one roar.

Controls

  • Camera — tap it to choose Max blur, Min blur, or No blur. Only you control your camera.
  • Hand — join the queue.
  • Password — the key to clear video.
  • Invite — one link brings people in.
  • Run app — an app the room uses together.
  • Record / CC — record here, or captions from your voice.
  • Settings — mix for Stage, My row, and the stadium. Timing: Conversation, Unison, or Song.
  • Admin — a host can moderate. Most rooms stay open.

Singing together

Tap Song to lead. You step onto the stage as the song leader, and the room lines up so you are singing together, like a large hall.

meet.setCcSendHelp: Your voice is written down while your mic is on and sent to the meeting as captions, so everyone can read you. Your browser's speech service (Google, Apple or Microsoft) hears your voice unless you pick Whisper below, which keeps it on this device. Off: the others' devices may still write you down.
meet.setCcSendCant: This browser has no speech engine, so it cannot send your captions. A device in the meeting that keeps a transcript writes you down instead.
meet.setTrOffHelp: Captions show on your screen when CC is on, and nothing is kept on this device.
meet.setTrKeepHelp: The usual setting. Every line is kept on this device, in the Transcript window, and can be downloaded. This device also writes down the people nobody is captioning, by name when it knows it, or as Stage or Stadium.
meet.setTrShare: Keep and share with the room
meet.setTrShareHelp: The same, and the lines this device writes about others go to everyone. Your tile shows a transcript badge.
meet.stSendingCaptionsOn: Sending your captions to the meeting.
meet.stSendingCaptionsOff: Your captions are off. The others may still write you down.
meet.stTranscriptShare: You keep a transcript and share the voices you write down with the room.
meet.stTranscriptKeep: You keep a transcript on this device.
meet.stTranscriptOff: No transcript is kept on this device.
meet.setDbgOnHelp: The log stays on this device and may include meeting details, such as names and chat or transcript text.
meet.setDbgClearAsk: Clear the whole debug log from this device?
meet.setDbgUrl: Recording on this page, because its link turned debug on.
meet.setDbgNext: Recording starts the next time a meeting page opens.
meet.setDbgExportFail: Could not export the debug log.
meet.setCcEnglishNeed: Needs Whisper installed: nothing is translated until it is.
meet.wspErrModel: its model could not be downloaded
meet.wspStUnsupported: Whisper: not supported on this browser
meet.wspRunNone: No captions are running from this device.
meet.stBrowserCaptionsOnWhisperOff: Browser captions are on. Whisper is off on this device.
